podcast.title: Appearance in The Ramones Video (1988)
podcast.body: Courtney Love made an appearance as one of the partiers in the background of The Ramones' 1988 music video for their song "I Want to Be Sedated," offering a glimpse into her early involvement in the music scene. "you can see her in the video of the Ramones made in 1988 for I Want to Be Sedated. She's one of the partiers in the background."

podcast.title: First Meeting with Kurt Cobain (1989)
podcast.body: Courtney Love first saw Kurt Cobain when Nirvana played at the Satiricon Club in Portland, Oregon, on January 21, 1989. Their initial interaction involved Kurt taking her pitcher of beer, and she developed a crush on him, with Kurt later remarking that she resembled Nancy Spungen. "Courtney Love first saw Kurt Cobain when Nirvana played a show at the Satiricon Club in Portland, Oregon. The day was January 21st, 1989."

podcast.title: Developing Relationship with Kurt Cobain (1991)
podcast.body: Courtney Love and Kurt Cobain "hooked up again" on May 29, 1991, at a Butthole Surfers show in Los Angeles, shortly after Nirvana signed their major deal. Their reunion was characterized by "instant attraction," escalating quickly from Courtney punching Kurt to wrestling and kicking, followed by sharing drugs such as Vicodin and high-powered cough syrup, resulting in them becoming "pretty much inseparable." "On May 29th, 1991, one month after Nirvana signed their major deal, Kurt and Courtney hooked up again at a butthole surfer show in Los Angeles."

podcast.title: Initiating Contact with Kurt Cobain (1991)
podcast.body: After their initial meeting in 1989, Courtney Love, a friend of Jennifer Finch (L7) and former girlfriend of Dave Grohl, learned through Dave that Kurt Cobain reciprocated her interest. She then sent Kurt a distinctive package containing seashells, pine cones, miniature teacups, and a doll, all presented in a heart-shaped box. "And one day Courtney told Dave that she liked Kurt and Dave told Courtney that Kurt kind of liked her. That's when she gave Dave a package to give to Kurt."

podcast.title: Alleged Murder-for-Hire Offer (1993)
podcast.body: Elden Hoke (Elduchet), singer for The Mentors, claimed in the April 1996 edition of High Times Magazine that in December 1993, Courtney Love offered him $50,000 to kill her husband, Kurt Cobain. Hoke quoted her as saying, "I need you to blow my old man's head off. I'll give you $50,000 to blow his effing head off." "Courtney Love offered him $50,000 to kill her husband."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Corroborated Meeting Location (1993)
podcast.body: Elden Hoke's claim about Courtney Love offering him money was partially corroborated by the owner of a record store called Rockshop on Wilcox Avenue in Los Angeles. Hoke stated Courtney pulled up in a limousine outside the store and exchanged car keys, a detail the owner confirmed. "The owner of the store corroborates Elduchet's story."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alleged Impersonation for Missing Person Report (April 4, 1994)
podcast.body: Private detective Tom Grant claimed that on April 4, 1994, Courtney Love filed a missing person's report for Kurt Cobain, pretending to be his mother, Wendy Cobain. Grant suggested this impersonation was done to strategically word the report, which stated Kurt "ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal," thereby influencing how police would approach the subsequent investigation. "It was Courtney that called that report in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alleged Overdose Story (1994)
podcast.body: After Kurt Cobain's disappearance from rehab, Courtney Love, who was in Los Angeles promoting a new Hole album, was reportedly "freaked out." She allegedly planted a story in the press claiming she had overdosed, theorizing that this would prompt Kurt to call her. "She allegedly planted a story in the press, saying that she overdosed."

podcast.body: Sometime on April 1, 1994, the day Kurt Cobain disappeared from rehab, Courtney Love had his MasterCard canceled. This action was later explained by her to Detective Tom Grant as an attempt to track Kurt's activities. "Sometime that day, she also had Kurt's master card canceled."

podcast.title: Cancellation of Kurt's Mastercard (April 1, 1994)

podcast.body: On March 4, 1994, in room 541 of the Excelsior Hotel in Rome, Courtney Love discovered Kurt Cobain in a coma after he ingested at least 50 Rohypnol tablets. She found him at 6:15 am, with blood coming from his nose and a suicide note and cash in his hands. Courtney promptly called an ambulance, and Kurt was subsequently revived 20 hours later. "Kurt slipped into a coma, but Courtney found him in time at 6.15am."

The alleged problem arose when the crew reportedly refused to allow her nurse into the first-class section where Love was seated, prompting the captain to radio ahead for police awaiting her on the tarmac. "The problem stemmed, allegedly, from the crew refusing to allow her nurse into where she was sitting in the first class section."

podcast.title: Reflections on Addiction (2011)
podcast.body: In a 2011 interview with The Fix, a publication on addiction and recovery, Love reflected on her drug experiences, stating that "kicking heroin really sucked" but "kicking coke was much easier." She recognized that cocaine was "not a good look" for her and admitted it was an "evil, evil drug" that "really effed me up in the head." She also noted that as she got older (46 at the time), one line of cocaine would lead to two days of depression, prompting her to seek other releases. "Kicking heroin really sucked. Kicking coke was much easier."

xref.body: Kurt Cobain died in the early morning of Tuesday, April 5, 1994, by suicide via shotgun, preceded by a massive heroin overdose. He seemed convinced to seek help and flew to LA on March 30 to check into the Exodus Recovery Center. However, he left on April 1 (Good Friday) by scaling a six-foot wall, flew back to Seattle, and disappeared. His final note, addressed to his imaginary friend "Boddah," was found in his pocket after he injected a large amount of Mexican black tar heroin and then used a Remington shotgun to kill himself in the greenhouse at his home. A nanny observed "way too much will talk" during this period. xref.title: Encounter with Duff McKagan and Death (1994)
xref.body: After escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain took Delta Flight 788 to Seattle and coincidentally sat next to Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan, also a veteran of rehab. Cobain refused a ride from McKagan upon landing, signed autographs, and disappeared. He then acquired drugs, returned to the room above the greenhouse at his and Courtney Love's Lake Washington Boulevard home, got high, and died by suicide, believed to be on April 5th, 1994. The news of his death broke on Friday, April 8th. "Soon, he was on Delta Flight 788 to Seattle, and by sheer coincidence, he was sitting next to Guns & Roses bass player Duff McAgan, himself, a junkie we have veteran."

Spending time with Courtney Love, it was concluded there was "no way" she was involved, and the theory was deemed unfounded. "in retrospect, I probably wouldn't have done the Kurt Cobain was murder thing because that turned out to be a bunch of conspiratorial garbage."

xref.title: Last House in Seattle
xref.body: Kurt Cobain's last residence was located at 171 Lake Washington Boulevard East in the Denny Blaine District of Seattle. This substantial house, measuring 7,000 square feet with four bedrooms, five bathrooms, and five fireplaces, was originally built in 1902 by Albert Blaine. Cobain's body was discovered in the greenhouse on the property in 1994, which Courtney Love subsequently had torn down in 1996. After Love sold the house in 1997, security measures like a large fence and cameras were installed, and more landscaping was added to preserve privacy. "Kurt Cobain's last house. The address is 171 Lake Washington Boulevard East in the Denny Blaine District of Seattle."

xref.title: Love Triangle with Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love
xref.body: In the early 1990s, a love triangle reportedly existed between Billy Corgan, Kurt Cobain, and Courtney Love. After Kurt Cobain's death, Corgan and Love briefly resumed a relationship. They subsequently broke up but later reunited for a two-year period beginning in 2006, creating "hard feelings" that have since reportedly dissipated. "For a while in the early 90s, there was something of a love triangle going on that also included Kurt Cobain."

xref.title: Medical Fetish – Anatomy Art, Gynecological Instruments, Full-Sized Medical Dummy on Tour
xref.body: Kurt Cobain's artistic aesthetic included a deep preoccupation with medical imagery and human anatomy that dated back to his grade school drawings. The artwork for *In Utero* features disassembled dolls, fetuses, and embryo-like forms. He reportedly collected vintage medical equipment and surgical instruments, including old gynecological devices well beyond basic medical tools. One account claims he kept a full-sized medical dummy at home and took it on tour in its own trunk. His journals (published by Courtney Love in 2002) reveal an obsession with bodily functions, vomit, urine, mucus, and excrement — consistent with his naming of his first band Fecal Matter. "Kurt had a full-sized medical dummy. Not only did he keep it around the house, but he toured with it."

xref.title: Nirvana Fatigue
xref.body: By early 1994, public fatigue with Nirvana had set in due to too much public complaining by Kurt Cobain, extensive drama surrounding Kurt and Courtney Love, and the commercial underperformance of their album *In Utero*. "Many people forget this, but Nirvana fatigue had set in. Too much complaining by Kurt, too much drama with Kurt and Courtney, and in utero, the follow-up to never mind had been a, well, a sales disappointment."

xref.body: Despite word spreading about the kind of music Sugar Baby Doll was attempting to create, there appear to be no surviving official recordings of the band. "Like I said, there doesn't seem to be any surviving official Sugar Baby Doll recordings."

xref.title: Post-Nirvana Feud with Courtney Love
xref.body: A significant feud developed between Dave Grohl and Courtney Love after Kurt Cobain's death. The first public evidence of bad blood was a 1999 interview where Dave Grohl, when asked for his favorite Hole song, replied "Teenage Horror" because it was "the one I know Courtney actually wrote," implying she didn't write others. Courtney Love subsequently attacked Dave in the media over legal disputes concerning Nirvana's music, accusing him of being sexually obsessed with Kurt Cobain and claiming he hired Taylor Hawkins as Foo Fighters' drummer because of Hawkins' resemblance to Kurt. "The first evidence I can find of some kind of bad blood was an interview Dave gave in 1999, a few years after the food fighters got going."

xref.title: Post-Sugar Baby Doll Collaboration
xref.body: After Sugar Baby Doll broke up in late 1985, Courtney Love and Cat Bjelland stayed together to form a new group called Pagan Babies. This band was another "pre-Riot Grrrl band" and, despite its brief existence, represents a link in the early collaborations of these influential musicians. "But when the band broke up in late 1985, Courtney and Cat stayed together long enough to be in a new group called Pagan Babies."

xref.title: Posthumous Business Deals
xref.body: Courtney Love sold a piece of the Nirvana Empire to Primary Wave, leading to increased merchandising like t-shirts, action figures, lunchboxes, and shoes, and the company now manages future licensing of Nirvana songs. Courtney also authorized the publication of Kurt's private diaries and was involved in the documentary "Montage of Heck." "Courtney sold a piece of the Nirvana Empire to a company called Primary Wave, which explains why we see more Kurt Cobain t-shirts and action figures and lunch boxes and shoes."

xref.title: Posthumous Financial Status and Beneficiaries
xref.body: Born February 27, 1967, and died April 5, 1994. Although already wealthy when alive, he became "even richer now that he's dead." His widow, Courtney Love, as the chief beneficiary of his estate, has utilized substantial funds for expenses such as a dog walker costing $100,000 annually and a PR firm costing $15,000 to $20,000 US per month. His daughter, Frances Bean, is also financially secure, having already received a pony. "Already rich when alive, even richer now that he's dead."
